source.filename: 2021-Nonlinear dynamic response of a wire rope isolator Experiment, identification and validation.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: The restoring and damping force of the isolator is modeled as the superposition of a linear elastic term, an asymmetric hysteretic term, an asymmetric cubic elastic term, and a viscous damping term.

The hysteretic restoring force follows an asymmetric Bouc-Wen formulation incorporating a pinching function and velocity-dependent control functions to eliminate non-physical asymmetric stiffness effects during unloading branches.
The uncontrolled structure is assumed to behave linearly as a single-degree-of-freedom clamped cantilever beam with tip mass and viscous material/boundary damping.
The isolated structure is modeled as a lumped-parameter two-degree-of-freedom system with the isolator in series with the two parallel cantilever beams.
control_variables: Cantilever beam dimensions: width of 30 mm, thickness of 2 mm, length of 7.5 cm
Lumped masses: 0.24 kg at each beam tip (0.48 kg total), 0.45 kg on the isolator support
Wire rope isolator specifications: 4 mm cable diameter with 7x7 construction of 0.4 mm stainless-steel wires
Vertical excitation direction corresponding to tension-compression mode
dependent_variables: Displacement response and displacement frequency response curves (FRCs)
Absolute acceleration response and acceleration frequency response curves (FRCs)
Transmissibility coefficients (H) for displacement and acceleration across frequency
Equivalent stiffness and equivalent hysteretic damping as functions of displacement amplitude
Restoring and damping force cycles (dynamic hysteresis loops)
Spectral harmonic and superharmonic components obtained via FFT

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A wire rope isolator demonstrates asymmetric hysteretic restoring force characterized by softening under compression and hardening under tension due to interwire friction and geometric cable nonlinearities.

A generalized asymmetric Bouc-Wen model with velocity-dependent control functions and asymmetric cubic polynomials accurately captures the hysteretic loops and removes asymmetric stiffness artifacts along unloading branches.
Parameters identified purely from quasi-static cyclic tests using a differential evolution algorithm are sufficient to predict the dynamic frequency response curves of the isolator.
Coupling the wire rope isolator to a flexible cantilever system reduces acceleration and displacement transmissibility by approximately an order of magnitude across a 5 to 100 Hz frequency band.

Asymmetry in the restoring force activates even superharmonics (such as 2:1 resonances at 7.5 Hz and 11.8 Hz) when dynamic oscillations exceed the static gravity deflection and cross into the positive displacement regime.
Even superharmonic excitations at high base acceleration levels can exceed primary resonances and channel energy directly into higher structural flexural modes, degrading isolation performance.
Maintaining the wire rope isolator under continuous compression throughout dynamic cycles suppresses the onset of even superharmonics and prevents superharmonic resonance amplification.

experimental_setup: Compact wire rope isolator comprising two metal plates joined by a 4 mm diameter stainless-steel wire rope (7x7 construction of 0.4 mm wires)
Two symmetric cantilever steel beams (30 mm wide, 2 mm thick, 7.5 cm long) carrying 0.24 kg tip masses, mounted on a 0.45 kg support mass
Electrodynamical shaker providing vertical base excitation across a frequency range of 5 Hz to 100 Hz
Four PCB Piezotronics accelerometers mounted on the beam tip masses, support mass, and shaker head
Signal conditioning using Savitzky-Golay filtering, double numerical integration, and high-pass filtering to evaluate velocities and displacements from acceleration data
Quasi-static cyclic loading tests at multiple displacement amplitudes (from 2.5 mm to 15 mm)
independent_variables: Excitation frequency (swept from 5 Hz to 100 Hz)
Base acceleration excitation amplitude (0.1 g, 0.25 g, 0.5 g, 0.75 g, 1.0 g, 1.25 g)
Structural isolation configuration (non-isolated vs. isolated structure)
limitations_inferred: Testing and identification are restricted to uniaxial vertical loading (tension-compression mode), omitting multi-axis coupling or combined shear-roll dynamics.
Model parameters identified under quasi-static rates were transferred directly to dynamic predictions without evaluating potential high-frequency or rate-dependent thermal and frictional changes.
The experimental structure was simplified to a stylized two-degree-of-freedom cantilever system, which may not capture multi-modal dynamics of complex machinery or robotic systems.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Wire rope isolators can experience substantial degradation in vibration isolation performance due to superharmonic resonances.

Asymmetric hysteretic behavior produces both odd and even superharmonics, causing unwanted multiplication and combination of superharmonic resonances when displacements expand into the positive displacement range.
Dynamic testing introduced a static equilibrium drift due to system weight, unlike the symmetric baseline in quasi-static cyclic tests.
main_results: The isolated system demonstrated an order-of-magnitude reduction in transmissibility over the 5–100 Hz range, reducing average transmissibility from approximately 75 in the non-isolated configuration to around 4 in the isolated configuration.

The device exhibited marked asymmetric stiffness, softening under compression and hardening under tension, with equivalent hysteretic damping displaying an overall decreasing trend with displacement amplitude.
Primary resonances of the isolated system occurred at approximately 14 Hz (isolator elongation mode) and 74 Hz (cantilever flexural mode), both displaying mild softening behavior.
Odd (3:1 at 24 Hz) and even (2:1 at 7.5 Hz and 11.8 Hz) superharmonic resonances were observed; at 1.0 g and 1.25 g, the 7.5 Hz superharmonic peak exceeded the primary resonance in amplitude.

Numerical predictions generated from the generalized Bouc-Wen model calibrated with quasi-static data matched experimental dynamic frequency response curves and superharmonic behaviors with high accuracy.
modeling_methods: Modified asymmetric Bouc-Wen hysteretic formulation with velocity-dependent control functions and asymmetric cubic polynomials
Differential evolution optimization algorithm for parameter identification from quasi-static cyclic test data
Lumped-parameter two-degree-of-freedom (2DOF) dynamic modeling using coupled second-order ordinary differential equations
Numerical time-domain integration of equations of motion and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) stationary response analysis
Analytical transfer function and closed-form frequency response function modeling for the linear uncontrolled cantilever structure
performance_metrics: Transmissibility coefficient (H) for displacement and absolute acceleration across 5–100 Hz
Peak displacement and acceleration amplitudes at primary and superharmonic resonances
Resonant frequency shift between non-isolated and isolated configurations
Equivalent secant stiffness and equivalent hysteretic damping across displacement amplitudes
Spectral power distribution of fundamental and superharmonic frequencies via FFT
possible_gap_implications: Demonstrates that asymmetric hysteretic elements provide high damping and transmissibility reduction, but designers must account for even superharmonics transferring energy to higher flexible modes when operating across tension-compression regimes.

The generalized Bouc-Wen modeling approach with velocity-dependent switching functions provides a potential framework for modeling asymmetric friction and hysteresis in cable-driven or tendon-actuated flexible structures.
paper.research_objective: To experimentally and numerically investigate the nonlinear dynamic response, asymmetric hysteretic behavior, and vibration isolation performance of a compact wire rope isolator in a two-degree-of-freedom structure under vertical base excitation, and to validate a generalized phenomenological Bouc-Wen model calibrated with quasi-static data.
paper.research_problem: Characterizing and predicting the nonlinear dynamic behavior and vibration isolation capabilities of wire rope isolators under vertical base excitation (tension-compression mode), specifically addressing asymmetric hysteresis, modeling unloading stiffness, and accounting for isolation performance loss caused by superharmonic resonances.
stiffness_mechanism: curved wire rope assembly undergoing interwire friction and geometric nonlinearities
asymmetric tension-compression stiffness exhibiting softening under compression and hardening under tension
tightening of spiral cable strands under tension and loosening under compression
paper.title: Nonlinear dynamic response of a wire rope isolator: Experiment, identification and validation
